<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Evaluating whether to centralize custom shortcodes under layouts/shortcodes/.

Hugo's lookup order means shortcodes in themes and vendor modules would override root layouts. Centralizing everything under layouts/shortcodes/ would require moving theme and Hugoplate vendor shortcodes too.

Hugoplate guidance supports this approach. Custom shortcodes belong in root layouts/shortcodes/. Theme shortcodes should be overridden there rather than edited directly in themes/. Vendor module shortcodes remain in their modules but can be customized by copying them to root layouts/.

Moving JoRap-owned theme shortcodes to root layouts/shortcodes/ follows Hugoplate's recommended pattern and keeps theme syncing cleaner.

Do not copy module shortcodes into layouts/ unless you intend to fork or override them. The youtube shortcode still overrides native Hugo regardless of its current location. The unused spotify.html may be deleted rather than moved. Check whether themes/jorap is a local fork of Hugoplate that should remain synced from upstream.
</details></think>

_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

Yes for **your** custom ones — not for the Hugoplate module ones.

**Move to `layouts/shortcodes/`:** the theme copies you own (`youtube`, `youtube_time`, `spotify*`). Root already beats theme, so behavior stays the same; you stop editing `themes/jorap/` and keep upstream theme sync cleaner.

**Leave alone:**
- `bible` / `card` — already at root
- Module shortcodes (`image`, `notice`, `accordion`, …) — stay in modules; only copy into `layouts/shortcodes/` if you need a real override

**Don’t centralize “everything”** into one folder by vendoring module templates — that forks Hugoplate and makes updates worse.

Worth doing when you next touch embeds or sync the theme; not urgent. Unused `spotify.html` is a delete candidate rather than a move.

_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

Most of the centralized custom shortcodes have **no separate CSS/JS**. Assets that do exist live under `assets/`, not next to the templates — and that’s the right place.

## Per shortcode

| Shortcode | CSS | JS |
|-----------|-----|-----|
| `youtube`, `youtube_time` | Inline styles in the template. Site has `.youtube-embed` in `assets/css/custom.css` / `custom-base.css`, but the shortcode defaults to class `youtube-video` — so that rule is unused. | None |
| `spotify`, `spotify_iframe_*` | Inline iframe attrs only | None |
| `bible` | `assets/css/notes-content.css` (`.scripture-verse`, `.jesus-words`, `.scripture-emphasis`, …) | None |
| `card` | `assets/css/notes-flashcards.css` (via `notes/flashcard` partial) | `assets/js/notes-flashcard.js` (loaded from notes layouts, not by the shortcode) |

`bible` markup itself is in `layouts/partials/shortcodes/bible.html`; the shortcode file is a thin wrapper.

## Module shortcodes (contrast)

Those ship assets under `_vendor/.../assets/` (and some theme `assets/js/`), loaded on demand by `layouts/_partials/essentials/conditional-plugins.html` when the page’s markdown mentions them (`accordion`, `tabs`, `gallery`, `youtube-lite`, …).

## Should CSS/JS live in `layouts/shortcodes/`?

**No.** Hugo only treats that folder as templates. CSS/JS belong in `assets/` so fingerprinting, bundling, and conditional loading keep working.

Co-locating would only make sense if a shortcode owned private assets *and* nothing else used them. Here:
- embeds are self-contained HTML
- `bible` / `card` share the notes garden design system

Keep templates in `layouts/shortcodes/`; leave styles/scripts in `assets/` (and notes partials).
